survey: A toy-style planetary rover shown in three-quarter view. The orange box body has a raised top plate. A dish antenna on a single steel post sits at the front left of the top plate; its feed is shown as a ball on a short stalk in the center of the dish. A small solar panel on one short post sits at the back right, tilted up toward the sky. The near side of the body has a bolted access panel, three vent slots and a side panel on the end face. The near-side suspension pivots from one round hub in the middle of the body side. Two long arms run from it to the hubs of the front and rear wheels. A short link with a knee joint drops from the hub to the middle wheel, which works as a simplified rocker-bogie. Three more wheels on the far side show behind the near ones, each offset back by the same perspective, so there are six wheels in all, matching the near side. A visible strut joins the far rear wheel to the body. All six tires sit on the grey ground with contact shadows, and the body clears the tops of the wheels.
